title: Mexicans
capsule: This entry appears to represent the insurgent Mexican nation-state identity coalescing between the Grito de Dolores of 16 September 1810—when Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla launched the independence movement—and the formal proclamation of independence in 1821 under Agustín de Iturbide's Plan of Iguala. In the intervening decade of warfare, insurgent leaders including Hidalgo, José María Morelos (who convened the Congress of Chilpancingo in 1813), and Vicente Guerrero fought the royalist army across New Spain without controlling a stable territorial state. The from-date of 1811 and to-date of 1820 bracket the middle phase of the insurgency, after Hidalgo's capture and execution (1811) and before Iturbide's realignment switched the royalist army to the independence cause.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The insurgent forces held no stable territory and their geographic footprint shifted constantly; territorial representation on a map is inherently approximate.
